author: CBR
description:
Spider-Man’s Captain America: Civil War debut created real behind-the-scenes tension at Marvel before the Sony deal was locked.

In this CBR Short, the directors explain how Captain America: Civil War caused a “civil war” inside Marvel. The film was already controversial because it turned Tony Stark, the MCU’s most popular hero at the time, into an antagonist against Steve Rogers. But bringing Spider-Man into Civil War made things even more complicated.

Marvel wanted Peter Parker in the story creatively, but Sony still controlled the movie rights to Spider-Man. That meant the MCU could only use Spider-Man through cooperation with Sony, and the filmmakers were developing the idea before a business agreement was fully in place. 

This quick Marvel breakdown explains why Spider-Man’s MCU debut was such a risky move, how it shaped Civil War, and why Tom Holland’s arrival as Peter Parker was a much bigger gamble than fans may realize.
